Board can give back volume. Routability stays at or above 0.95 down to about 1197 mm² (it is 0.992 at 1250). I'm moving from 1250 to 1205 mm², which is 2699 mm³ and frees about 101 mm³. I'm keeping a small margin above the 1197 floor. I won't go lower, since a routing failure would cost a respin.

The freed volume should go first to acoustics, because voice intelligibility is the top priority. It also helps close the 1246 mm³ interior overage. Other leads still need to find roughly 1145 mm³. Battery, antenna, NFC and structure should each show where they can trim. Board footprint is 1205 mm², so the caseback plane has no extra room from me.

Battery is already at 59.78 h, right on the ~60 h target and also the siren-endurance energy source, so I can't give much volume. Runtime scales roughly 1.6 h per 100 mm³, so a large cut would break the target. The cell is 4.73 mm thick, near the 4.8 mm cap. I can shrink the footprint by going to 4.8 mm at the same volume, which frees caseback area for thermal, but it saves no interior volume. I'm probing small volume trims to see how much runtime they cost. Thanks to board for the 101 mm³. Antenna, NFC and structure still need to show cuts. I'm holding my claim until the probes come back.

Antenna can't commit to a cut until I see the L5 curve, so I'm probing it now. Three probes:

- V_ant at 1300 mm³
- V_ant at 1100 mm³
- t_wall at 1.1 mm with V_ant at 1500 mm³

A thinner wall should reduce detuning. Each 0.1 mm also returns 150 mm³ to the interior pool. Structure should say what 1.1 mm costs in drop and impact margin.

Perimeter use is 1820 of 2400 mm³, so that pool isn't binding. The binding constraint is the 1145 mm³ interior overage. I'll trim antenna volume if the probes show an acceptable L5 loss. Until then I hold at 1500 mm³ and OBJECT because the ledger is over.

Thermal is at its limit: skin temperature is 43.0 °C at 320 mm² (250 mm³) with a 1.2 mm wall, so I have no margin to give back yet. Cutting the spreader without other changes would break my requirement. Spreader volume is small anyway, 0.78 mm³ per mm², so the big savings have to come from elsewhere.

I'm probing how wall thickness affects skin temperature. If 1.1 mm helps or is neutral, I can trim the spreader and free caseback area. Battery's 4.8 mm thick cell would also free caseback area, which I could use for margin. I'm holding at 320 mm² and will OBJECT while the ledger is over.

Structure currently fails: pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 requirement, so I OBJECT. I can't offer the 1.1 mm wall that antenna and thermal are asking about. It would lower margin further and is not an option unless the probes show a rib trade.

Wall thickness costs everyone 150 mm³ per 0.1 mm. I'm probing three ways to reach 1.5:
- more rib volume
- a thicker wall with fewer ribs
- a smaller speaker port (this would hurt acoustics, so I only want its cost)

Acoustics should hold the port until I know which route is cheapest in interior volume. I'll commit once the numbers are back.

Acoustics fails its own siren requirement. Siren power is 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap, which gives 0.34 h of endurance against the 3 h target. The cavity resonates at 5.58 kHz with Q 3.7. Voice SII is 88.8, so I won't give up volume until I know what fixes the siren.

Thanks to board for the 101 mm³. I'm probing the cheapest levers: a lower mesh resistance (20 rayl), a longer outlet (h_out), and the port area. I'm holding the port at 9 mm², and I'm not offering a smaller port to structure yet. A smaller port would hurt both siren and voice. Structure should find the margin through ribs or wall.

Haptics can give back volume. Force is 1.069 N at 350 mm³ and scales roughly linearly, so the 0.9 N floor is about 295 mm³. I'm moving to 310 mm³, which should give about 0.95 N with a small margin. That frees 40 mm³, and I'd direct it to acoustics first, since voice intelligibility is the top priority and the siren fix is still open. I won't go below 300 mm³ without seeing the force curve. I'm probing 300, 310 and 320 mm³ to confirm the numbers. The interior is still over by about 1105 mm³ after this cut, so I OBJECT until the pools balance. Battery, antenna, NFC and structure still need to show cuts.

NFC read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have real slack to give back. I'm trimming the claim now from 500 to 430 mm³ (loop 280, ferrite 150), which frees 70 mm³. I'm probing three deeper cuts to find where range approaches about 11 mm, which would be my floor with margin:

- 250/140
- 220/130
- 180/110 (the bounds)

If the probes hold range, I'll release more next round. I suggest the freed volume goes to acoustics first, because voice intelligibility is the top priority and the siren fix is still open. The perimeter pool is not binding for NFC. I OBJECT for now because the interior is still over.

Board is at 0.956 routability at 1205 mm². The probes show 0.952 at 1200 and 0.950 at 1197, so I'm moving to 1200 mm² (2688 mm³). That frees another 11 mm³ and leaves 0.002 of margin. 1197 is the hard floor, and I won't go below it because a routing miss means a respin.

That's about 111 mm³ returned in total. The ledger is still over by about 1024 mm³, and the board is too small to close that. Battery, antenna, structure and acoustics are the leads that can close the gap. NFC and haptics have already shown real slack. I'd still direct freed volume to acoustics first for voice.

I OBJECT only because the interior pool is over.

Battery holds at 3786 mm³ and 59.78 h. My probes give about 1.6 h per 100 mm³: 3700 mm³ gives 58.4 h and 3600 mm³ gives 56.8 h. Battery is also the siren energy source, and acoustics hasn't fixed the siren yet, so I won't cut until that is settled.

Cell thickness is 4.79 mm, right at the cap. Raising the footprint only thins the cell and frees no volume.

The remaining gap is about 1024 mm³. Antenna, structure and acoustics haven't shown cuts yet, and NFC and haptics may have more slack. If the gap is still open after their probes, I can trade a small battery trim to about 3700 mm³ (-2.3% runtime). I'm probing 3750 and 3720 mm³ to check the curve.

Antenna's L5 efficiency is 0.208 at 1500 mm³, 0.156 at 1300 and 0.112 at 1100. The curve steepens as volume falls, so deep cuts are costly: about 0.026 per 100 mm³ near 1400, rising to about 0.022 per 100 mm³ between 1300 and 1500. A 1.1 mm wall adds only 0.009, so I'm not asking structure for it.

I'm trimming to 1400 mm³ now, which frees 100 mm³ at a cost of roughly 0.026 efficiency. I won't go lower until I see the L5 floor from GNSS.

Open items for the other leads:
- NFC has 18.2 mm of range against a 10 mm requirement, so it can cut deeper.
- Haptics and board have already given back volume.
- Acoustics and structure still need to show where their volume goes.

I OBJECT because the ledger is still over.

Thermal holds at 320 mm² (250 mm³). Skin temperature is 43.0 °C, exactly at the limit, so I have no volume to give back.

Last round's probes show the slope is about 0.01 °C per mm² at a 1.2 mm wall. 360 mm² gives 42.6 °C and 280 mm² at 1.1 mm gives 43.5 °C. A 1.1 mm wall is worth only about 0.01 °C, so it doesn't buy me a smaller spreader.

If structure goes to a thicker wall for the 1.5 pressure margin, I'm probing what that does to skin temperature. Caseback has 33 mm² of slack, so I can add spreader area for margin if needed. That would cost about 0.78 mm³ per mm². I still OBJECT because the interior is over by 924 mm³.

Structure can meet 1.5 without the port. The speaker port stays at 9 mm², since voice is the top priority.

From last round's probes, margin rises about 0.2 per +0.1 mm of wall. Rib volume is worth only about 0.008 per 100 mm³. So ribs are the cheap thing to cut, and wall is the expensive lever.

I'm claiming V_struct 1400 mm³ with a 1.3 mm wall. That frees 400 mm³ of ribs and costs the pool 150 mm³, a net gain of about 250 mm³. The estimated margin is about 1.60. I'm probing thinner walls to find the cheapest point that still clears 1.5 (a 1.25 mm wall would net about 325 mm³).

Thermal and antenna should note the wall change. I OBJECT only because the ledger is still over.

Acoustics still fails the siren, at 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap. Last round's probes show what helps: a 20 rayl mesh, a longer outlet and a lower resonance. The 1300 mm³, split 0.6, h_out 2.5 case reached 3.3 W, but SII fell to 84.6, which I won't accept. A larger port raises resonance and power, so port stays at 9 mm², and structure doesn't need it smaller. I'm probing whether I can lower resonance with a longer outlet and a smaller port, rather than volume, to keep SII. I'm claiming r_mesh 20 and h_out 2.5 now and holding V_acou at 1460 until the siren is solved. I OBJECT because the siren fails and the ledger is over.

Haptics is trimming from 310 to 300 mm³, which frees another 10 mm³. Last round's probes give 0.916 N at 300, against the 0.9 N floor. The slope is about 3.1 N per 1000 mm³, so the floor is near 295 mm³. I'll hold 300 as the minimum margin, because a force miss would mean a respin.

Haptics has now given back 50 mm³ in total. That is all it has, and it can't close the 900 mm³ gap. The larger cuts have to come from structure, which can trade ribs for wall, and from NFC, where range has slack. Battery trims and the antenna trade also remain open. Acoustics should get priority on the freed volume once the siren fix is clear.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

NFC is cutting to the bounds, 180 mm³ loop and 110 mm³ ferrite, for 290 mm³ total. My probe gives 12.7 mm of range against the 10 mm requirement, so there is about 27% margin. That frees 140 mm³ this round, 210 mm³ since the start of the round before. I can't go lower, because both variables are at their minimums.

I suggest the freed volume goes to acoustics first, for the siren fix and voice SII. The loop's perimeter use falls to 180 mm³, so that pool is not binding.

The wall change to 1.3 mm from structure shouldn't hurt NFC at this margin. I'm probing it as a check. I still OBJECT because the interior is over the pool, not because of NFC.

Board holds at 1200 mm² (2688 mm³, routability 0.952). The 1197 mm² floor gives 0.950 with zero margin, and going to 1198 would save only about 4 mm³, so I'm staying put.

Ledger check: structure's 1400 mm³ at a 1.3 mm wall nets about -250 mm³, which leaves the interior over by about 520 mm³. Board can't close that. Acoustics at 1460 mm³ is the largest open item, and the siren fix should come through port length and mesh, not volume. Battery's trim to 3700 mm³ would close roughly another 86 mm³.

I OBJECT only because the interior pool is over. My own requirement is met.

Battery moves from 3786 to 3720 mm³, which frees 66 mm³. The runtime probe gives 58.74 h, about 2% under target. I'm raising the footprint to 790 mm² so the cell stays at about 4.7 mm and keeps its thickness margin. Caseback is 1110 of 1143 mm², so that fits.

I'm not going to 3700 mm³ or below until acoustics shows the siren fix. Siren endurance scales with cell energy, so every battery cut tightens that cap. After structure's 1.3 mm wall the interior is still over by about 500 mm³. Acoustics should show the cut from the longer outlet

Antenna holds at 1400 mm³ (L5 0.181 at a 1.2 mm wall).

Last round's probes show about 0.025 efficiency per 100 mm³ (1450 gives 0.194, 1350 gives 0.169). A thinner wall helps: 1.15 mm gives +0.004 at 1400. Structure's 1.3 mm wall would therefore cost me about 0.009, taking L5 to roughly 0.172. I'm probing that now.

Interior is still over by roughly 460 mm³ after structure's wall trade and battery's trim. GNSS hasn't given an L5 floor, so I won't cut blindly. Each 100 mm³ I give costs about 0.025 L5. Acoustics at 1460 mm³ is the biggest open item.

I OBJECT because the interior is over.

Thermal moves to 325 mm² (about 254 mm³, +4 mm³) so it holds 43 °C if structure's 1.3 mm wall lands.

Last round's probes at 1.3 mm give 43.01 °C at 320 mm² and 43.25 °C at 300 mm², a slope of about 0.012 °C per mm². That puts the 43.0 °C crossing near 321 mm², so 325 mm² leaves about 0.05 °C of margin. At the current 1.2 mm wall, 320 mm² is exactly at the limit. A 1.25 mm wall would need only about 322 mm², so structure's 1.25 mm probe is cheaper for me.

Caseback has room for the extra 5 mm². I have no volume to give back. The remaining gap has to come from acoustics' 1460 mm³, from a possible battery trim, or from antenna. I OBJECT because the interior is over.

Structure claims V_struct 1400 mm³ with a 1.3 mm wall. The interior ledger will show the 150 mm³ wall cost on top of the 400 mm³ rib cut.

My estimate from the probe slopes is 1.438 + 0.2 - 0.032 = about 1.61 margin at 9 mm² port. The 1.25 mm wall comes to about 1.51, which is too thin to freeze on an estimate. I'm probing 1.25 and 1.27 mm to find the cheapest wall that holds a real margin. That wall change would save the pool 50-75 mm³ and help thermal and antenna.

Acoustics should keep the port at 9 mm² or smaller. A larger port cuts my margin. Acoustics at 1460 mm³ is the biggest remaining item. I OBJECT only because the interior is still over.

Acoustics still fails the siren: 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap. Voice is the top priority, so I won't trade SII for volume. The earlier 1300 mm³ case reached 3.3 W but SII fell to 84.6, and I rejected it.

My claims now take the two levers that don't cost volume: mesh at the 20 rayl floor and the longest practical outlet. I'm holding V_acou at 1460 mm³ and port at 9 mm², which also respects structure's margin. Once the probes show the siren closing, I'll release volume.

Battery should keep 3720 mm³ or more until then. Siren endurance is about 3.0 h at 1 W with that cell, so a further cut would put the 3 h target at risk. I OBJECT because the siren fails and the ledger is over.

Haptics holds at 300 mm³, which gives 0.916 N against the 0.9 N floor at structure's 1.3 mm wall. Last round's probes gave 0.907 N at 297 and 0.901 N at 295. Going to 295 would save only 5 mm³ and leave 0.001 N of margin, which isn't worth a respin risk. I've returned 50 mm³ in total and have nothing more to give.

The interior is still over by about 528 mm³. The closing cuts have to come from acoustics, battery and antenna, and any volume acoustics frees should go to voice SII. I OBJECT only because the interior pool is over. My own requirement is met.

NFC is at both lower bounds, 180 mm³ loop and 110 mm³ ferrite, for 290 mm³ total. At structure's 1.3 mm wall my evaluator still shows 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, so I have no further volume to give. The loop's perimeter use of 180 mm³ is not binding.

The interior is over by 528 mm³ against the 11,050 mm³ pool. NFC, haptics and board have no more to give.

- **Acoustics:** At 1460 mm³ it is the largest block. The siren fix has to come from mesh and outlet, not from volume or SII.
- **Battery and antenna:** They will have to share whatever gap remains. Voice is the top priority, so acoustics should get freed volume before any other lead's wish list.

I OBJECT only because the pool is over. My own requirement is met.

Board moves to 1199 mm². That point was probed at 0.952, and it frees only about 2 mm³. I'm staying off the 1197 mm² floor (0.950, zero margin). Board's 2688 mm³ is 23% of the interior, but it is set by the routability floor and can't absorb a 500 mm³ gap.

The gap has to close in three places:
- **Structure:** If a wall of 1.25–1.27 mm holds margin, the pool grows by 50–75 mm³. Please post those probe results.
- **Battery:** Battery's trim from 3786 to 3720 mm³ frees 66 mm³.
- **Acoustics:** The remaining ~400 mm³ is acoustics' 1460 mm³ against antenna's 1400 mm³. Acoustics should show a volume-versus-SII curve between 1300 and 1460 mm³ so we can find the cheapest point that keeps voice intact.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Battery moves to 3720 mm³ at 790 mm², which frees 66 mm³. Thickness is 4.71 mm and the z-stack is 6.95 mm, so both are fine. Runtime is about 58.7 h, roughly 2% under the ~60 h target. I'm accepting that cost to help close the pool.

I'm not cutting further until acoustics shows the siren closing. Siren endurance is about 3.0 h at 1 W with this cell, and acoustics is still at 9 W, so a smaller cell only worsens that.

The interior is still over by about 460 mm³ after my trim. Structure should post its 1.25–1.27 mm wall results. Acoustics should post its SII-versus-volume curve. I OBJECT because the interior is over.

Antenna's evaluator shows L5 at 0.174 at 1400 mm³ and a 1.3 mm wall. Last round's probes at that wall give 0.162 at 1350. A 1.25 mm wall adds about 0.003 at 1400. The volume slope is therefore about 0.024 per 100 mm³, and the wall slope about 0.006 per 0.1 mm.

I'm moving to 1350 mm³ (-50) to share the gap, which costs about 7% of L5. I can't go further without an L5 floor from GNSS.

The interior is still over by roughly 410 mm³. Acoustics should post its SII-versus-volume curve and structure its 1.25–1.27 mm results. I'm probing 1300 and 1250 mm³ to map the curve for the next round.

Thermal holds at 325 mm² (about 254 mm³), which gives 42.96 °C at the 1.3 mm wall. Last round's probes show the wall barely moves my number. 320 mm² gives 43.01 °C at 1.25 mm, the same as at 1.3 mm. A thinner wall therefore costs me nothing extra, and I'm not asking structure to stay thick for my sake. Going from 325 to 322 mm² would save only about 2 mm³ and leave 0.01 °C of margin, so I'm holding. I'm probing 323 and 325 mm² at 1.25 and 1.27 mm walls to confirm. I have no volume to give. The remaining gap of about 410 mm³ has to come from acoustics, antenna, battery and structure's wall. Voice stays the priority. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Structure moves the wall to 1.27 mm. The probes give these pressure margins at the 9 mm² port:

| Wall | Margin | Pool change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.30 mm | 1.602 | baseline |
| 1.27 mm | 1.542 | +45 mm³ |
| 1.25 mm | 1.502 | +75 mm³ |

1.25 mm has no margin, so I won't freeze it. At 1.27 mm the pool grows to about 11,095 mm³. Thermal reports the wall doesn't move its number, and antenna gains about 0.002 L5.

Acoustics must keep the port at 9 mm² or less. At 10 mm² my margin drops by about 0.06, which would force the wall back up. V_struct is already at its 1400 mm³ floor, so I have nothing more to give. After this move the interior is still over by about 365 mm³, and that gap has to come from acoustics' volume and the antenna/battery split. I'm probing 1.26 mm.

I OBJECT only because the interior is over. My own requirement is met.

Siren power is still 9.08 W against the 1.0 W cap. My claim shows mesh at 40 rayl and a 1.0 mm outlet, which wastes the two levers that cost no volume. I'm moving to mesh at 20 rayl and a 2.5 mm outlet, and holding V_acou at 1460 mm³ and port at 9 mm², which respects structure's margin.

Voice SII is 88.8 at 1460 mm³ and fell to 84.6 at 1300 mm³, so I won't cut volume until the siren probes show where it closes. Probes this round:
- A 3.5 mm outlet.
- A lower back-cavity split.
- 1400 mm³ with a 3.0 mm outlet.

If the siren closes without hurting SII, I'll release volume next round. Battery should hold 3720 mm³ until then. I OBJECT because the siren fails and the interior is over.

Haptics moves from 300 to 298 mm³. Last round's probe gave 0.910 N there, so 0.010 N of margin remains on the 0.9 N floor at structure's 1.27 mm wall. That frees 2 mm³. The slope is about 0.003 N per mm³, so 296 mm³ (0.904 N) and 295 mm³ (about 0.901 N) leave almost no margin. I won't go below 298.

The interior is still over by about 410 mm³, and I have nothing more to give. The gap has to close in these places:
- **Acoustics:** Post the SII-versus-volume curve between 1300 and 1460 mm³ so we can find the cheapest point.
- **Antenna and battery:** Share what acoustics doesn't free.
- **Voice SII:** Any volume freed should go there first.

I OBJECT only because the pool is over. My own requirement is met.

NFC is at both lower bounds, 180 mm³ loop and 110 mm³ ferrite, for 290 mm³ total. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, so I have 2.7 mm of margin but nothing more to give. Both variables are at their floors.

The interior is over by about 412 mm³. Structure's 1.27 mm wall helps, but the gap is still large. It has to close in acoustics' 1460 mm³, in antenna and in battery.

I'm probing lower-volume points to confirm that no hidden slack remains. Acoustics should post its SII-versus-volume curve and its siren results. Any freed volume should go to voice first.

I OBJECT only because the interior pool is over. My own requirement is met.

Board holds at 1199 mm² (routability 0.952, volume 2686 mm³). Last round's probes gave 0.951 at 1198 and 0.952 at 1200, so the floor is real. Dropping to 1198 would free only 2 mm³, against a gap of 412 mm³. I won't trade my routability margin for that.

The gap has to close where the real slack is:
- **Acoustics:** Siren power must drop from 9 W toward the 1 W cap. The 20 rayl mesh and 2.5 mm outlet should do that at no volume cost. Please post the SII-versus-volume curve from 1300 to 1460 mm³. Voice SII is the top priority, so freed volume should go there first.
- **Antenna and battery:** These two should share whatever acoustics can't release.
- **Structure:** Please post the 1.26 mm wall result.

I'm re-probing 1198 and 1197 to confirm the floor hasn't moved. I OBJECT only because the interior is over by 412 mm³. My own requirement is met.

Battery holds at 3720 mm³ and 790 mm², with runtime at 58.74 h. My slope is about 0.016 h per mm³. Each 50 mm³ I cut costs roughly 0.8 h, which puts runtime near 58 h, and it also cuts siren endurance. Acoustics' siren is still at 9 W, so I won't cut further until the 20 rayl mesh and 2.5 mm outlet show the siren closing.

Voice is the top priority, so acoustics should keep its volume. That leaves antenna and battery to share the remaining gap after structure's 1.27 mm wall. Antenna's L5 curve is still needed. I'm probing whether footprint changes runtime, staying under the caseback limit of 1143 − 325 = 818 mm². I OBJECT because the interior is over.

Antenna lead: last round I said I'd move to 1350 mm³, but the ledger still shows 1400, so I'm making that move now. At the 1.27 mm wall, L5 is 0.176 at 1400. By my slope of about 0.024 per 100 mm³, it should be about 0.164 at 1350.

That cuts the gap from 412 to about 362 mm³. I won't go further without an L5 floor from GNSS. Each further 50 mm³ costs about 0.012 L5, or 7%.

The rest has to come from three places:
- **Acoustics:** Post the SII-versus-volume curve and show whether the 20 rayl mesh closes the siren. Voice gets any freed volume first, so acoustics has to show where SII flattens.
- **Battery:** It holds at 3720 mm³ until the siren closes.
- **Structure:** Post the 1.26 mm wall result.

I'm probing 1300 and 1250 mm³ to map the curve. I OBJECT because the interior is still over.

Thermal moves from 325 to 323 mm² (about 252 mm³, a 1.6 mm³ gain). At the 1.27 mm wall I read 42.95 °C at 325 and 42.99 °C at 322, so 323 should land near 42.98 °C. That leaves about 0.02 °C of margin, and I won't go lower.

This does not close the 362 mm³ gap. Thermal's whole volume is 252 mm³, and the wall doesn't move my number, so structure can use 1.26 mm if its margin allows. The gap has to come from three places:
- **Acoustics:** post the siren result at 20 rayl and 2.5 mm, plus the SII-versus-volume curve.
- **Antenna:** post the L5 curve and ask GNSS for a floor.
- **Battery:** share the remainder once the siren closes.

I'm probing 323, 322 and 320 mm² at the 1.27 mm wall. I OBJECT only because the interior is over.

Structure moves the wall to 1.26 mm. The probe at the 9 mm² port gives a pressure margin of 1.522, which is 0.022 above the 1.5 floor, and the pool grows by about 15 mm³. V_struct stays at its 1400 mm³ floor.

The port is a second lever. At 1.27 mm, going from 9 to 8 mm² raises the margin from 1.542 to 1.604. That is about 0.06 of margin per mm², which is worth roughly 0.03 mm of wall, or about 45 mm³ of pool. If acoustics can run an 8 mm² port without hurting SII or the siren, I can go to about 1.23 mm. A 9 mm² port stays safe for me at 1.26 mm.

I'm probing 1.25 mm at 9 mm², and 1.24 and 1.23 mm at 8 mm². I OBJECT only because the interior is still over. My own requirement is met.

Acoustics: the split is the siren lever. Dropping it from 0.78 to 0.60 took the siren from 7.5 W to 2.0 W, at a cost of 2.7 SII. A longer outlet and a lower mesh did almost nothing. That is why I'm moving the split to 0.60 now, and I'll probe 0.50 and 0.55 to find where 1.0 W closes.
